bc_amo_wall.blurb: AMO Wall is a slab crag just north of Shannon Falls near Squamish, British Columbia. It holds nine bolted climbs, with multi-pitch lines of up to four pitches. Grades are mostly moderate, from 5.7 through the low 5.10s, with a single 5.11 and one very easy line at the bottom end. It is a handy place to practise friction and smearing before moving on to bigger slabs. Bolt spacing is mostly decent, though a few pitches have run-outs. The wall sits in thick forest, and heavy vegetation makes the lines hard to pick out from the ground.

bc_gobsmacking_wall.blurb: Gobsmacking Wall is the southern end of the Shannon Falls cliffs near Squamish, British Columbia. It climbs out of the lower slabs as a steep vertical wall with overhangs that have square-cut edges. All nine routes are trad, split between the 5.10 and 5.11 range, so it suits climbers already comfortable on harder crack and face climbing. Pitches run roughly 20 to 45 m, several routes have more than one pitch, and some pitches can be linked into longer ones. Much of the wall saw little traffic for years, though new lines and refurbished older ones have appeared lately.

bc_blipvert.blurb: Blipvert is a narrow tower in the Doctors' Group at Skaha Bluffs, in the Okanagan of British Columbia. Of its nine routes, seven are sport and two are trad. Grades mostly sit in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a single 5.10 and one 5.7 for contrast, so it mainly suits climbers on harder terrain. The tower faces west and stands in a tight gully, which keeps it shaded longer in the morning than other west-facing walls. Lines are long: the lower wall is fingery, and the upper face bulges for a sustained pump.
bc_blipvert.approach: Walk to Doctors' Wall, then carry on north to the split in the rocks at the north end. Blipvert is the left-hand tower there, with a small talus field spreading from its base.

bc_gamma_wall.blurb: Gamma Wall is one of the harder walls in Cougar Canyon, on the eastern shore of Kalamalka Lake near Vernon, British Columbia. It faces south, is overhung, and dries quickly, which makes spring and fall good times to visit. Eight of the nine routes are sport and one is trad, with grades running from an easy 5.6 up through the 5.10s and 5.11s, most of them 5.10 or 5.11. The canyon rock is gneiss, grainier and more textured than the stone at Skaha. Getting in involves a scramble down a gully to a cable traverse.
